title: Prevent KV thrashing and mixed-length batch starvation causing intermittent latency spikes
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Summary: Multiple customer escalations (Hosted + Dedicated + Private) report periodic short-request latency spikes that coincide with large long-context requests. We observe bursts where small, latency-sensitive requests wait tens to hundreds of milliseconds while the scheduler prioritizes or batches around long-context work, and the KV cache churns. This ticket tracks the investigation, root-cause fixes, and rollout for a kernel- and scheduler-level mitigation to prevent KV thrashing and mixed-length batch starvation.

Impact: Reproducible on production clusters serving mixed workloads; affects real-time features (chat quick replies, embeddings) for 3 enterprise customers and several Hosted customers during peak windows. Customer impact: high.

Reproduction steps (internal):
1) Run mixed workload harness (short 16-token requests at 200 rps + occasional 8k token requests at 1-2 rps) against a dedicated pool.
2) Observe scheduler logs and batch composition; enable kv-cache metrics and sequence eviction events.
3) Notice periodic windows where small-request latency distribution P50/P95 jumps and KV eviction_rate spikes.

Root cause hypothesis: The continuous batcher groups requests by arrival and waits for batch windows; long-context requests expand batch time and cause backend kernel runs that evict/overwrite KV cache segments. When eviction is synchronous or forces preemption, inflight short requests are delayed and subsequent small batches are starved until cache stabilizes. Additionally, our preemption heuristics sometimes pick long requests over queued short requests because of weight estimation errors.

Proposed plan:
- Short-term hotfix (canary to runtime-1.22): implement an admission heuristic that marks short, latency-sensitive requests with a higher preemption priority and forces small-batch fast-path (no KV eviction allowed during scheduling).
- Medium-term: add KV cache affinity — keep hot KV pages pinned for tenant-local short flows and add soft cap on per-worker KV eviction rate.
- Scheduler improvement: refine weight estimation to account for predicted token growth for long requests and add a micro-scheduling window (max 3ms) that ensures short-request dispatches are not delayed by single long-request batch formation.
- Observability: add a per-request KV evictions counter, batch composition histogram, and an alert on >10% small-request starvation windows per 5m.

Testing and rollout: unit + integration harnesses in CI, deterministic sim tests for mixed workloads, canary on 5% of dedicated pools and 2 Hosted regions, ramp to 50% after 48hrs stable, full rollout on success. Rollback plan: toggle off admission heuristic via runtime flag and revert scheduler weight change.

Stakeholders and owners: Eng runtime (Ethan Zhou lead), SRE (Liam O'Connor for canary ops), Product (Sara Kim) for customer comms, Support (Olivia Reyes) to coordinate escalations.

Artifacts: design doc draft: https://confluence.company/realtime/scheduler-kv-fix-draft, reproducer harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/repro-harness/pull/202, initial PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5187

Acceptance criteria: 1) No reproducible P95 spike for short requests in reproducer; 2) Production canary shows <10% of pre-fix starvation windows; 3) No regression on throughput for long-context workloads beyond 5%.
